answers.answer: They cannot win on the turn they take the title in Act. At the start of their next turn's Wake, they are still Oathkeeper: check Exile Usurper/Visionary wins first, then flip an Exile Oathkeeper to Usurper. They can first win at the next Exile Wake check after that flip, or at the end of round 8 if that arrives first and they still hold the title. Losing the title prevents the Usurper win; retaking it makes it Oathkeeper again and restarts the sequence.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions, Usurper victory: next Wake check, then flip, then win at following Wake or round 8; losing title prevents win and retaking resets.

answers.answer: Supremacy matches Conquest; People matches Rebellion; Protection matches Sanctuary; Devotion matches Faith. For a Visionary win, an Exile must have the true Vision revealed, meet its goal at Wake, and at least 3 Visions must have been drawn from the world deck by all players combined. A Vision's 'most' goal (Conquest or Sanctuary) requires strictly more than every other player; ties do not count.
answers.evidence: Oathkeeper title and four Oaths table; Visionary victory paragraph.

answers.answer: At the ends of rounds 5, 6, and 7, roll only if Chancellor or a Citizen is Oathkeeper. The game ends on 6 in round 5, 5–6 in round 6, or 3–6 in round 7. The Chancellor wins unless a Citizen meets the Successor goal, in which case that Citizen wins alone. An Exile Oathkeeper/Usurper prevents the roll, so an Exile Oathkeeper cannot permit it.
answers.evidence: Stable regime paragraph: end-of-round timing, results, winners, and Exile title prevents roll.

answers.answer: Round 8 ends automatically. Priority: (1) if Chancellor or Citizen is Oathkeeper, Empire wins, with a qualifying Citizen Successor winning alone instead of Chancellor; (2) otherwise an Exile Usurper wins; (3) otherwise a qualifying revealed Exile Vision wins, with simultaneous qualifying Visions ordered Conquest, Rebellion, Sanctuary, Faith; (4) otherwise Empire wins, with a qualifying Citizen Successor replacing the Chancellor, even if an Exile is Oathkeeper. Successor status alone does not end the game.
answers.evidence: War exhaustion list, steps 1–4; following sentence says Successor goal never ends game by itself.

answers.answer: Supremacy: hold more relics plus banners than the Chancellor and every other Citizen. People: hold Darkest Secret. Protection: hold People's Favor. Devotion: hold Grand Scepter. Citizens and Chancellor cannot win by true Vision or Usurper.
answers.evidence: Oathkeeper title and four Oaths table; Visionary victory paragraph.

answers.answer: At Wake, if you hold People's Favor, either place 1 favor from your board on it or return 1 favor from it to a least-full suit bank (choose among tied banks). If it has 1 favor, you may not remove its last favor; you must add one if able, otherwise do nothing. If it is already Mob-side, make this choice twice. After the choice(s), check whether it has at least 6 favor and flip it to Mob. If it becomes Mob at this check, that does not trigger an extra payment during the same Wake.
answers.evidence: Wake, mandatory order, People's Favor: payment choice, last-favor constraint, repeat on Mob side, then 6+ flip with no retroactive repeat.

answers.answer: Rest order: return favor on denizens/edifices to matching suit banks; return secrets on denizens/edifices/relics to your board and flip facedown secrets on your board faceup; refresh Supply; save unspent Supply; then resolve optional Rest powers, each once in chosen order. Exile/Chancellor refresh based on warbands remaining in their personal bank. Citizens refresh to exactly the Chancellor marker space, including leftmost, without counting purple warbands. Move the marker one extra space left for each unspent Supply, capped at leftmost (7 Supply).
answers.evidence: Rest, mandatory order, steps 1–5; Citizen uses exact Chancellor marker space and saved Supply rule.

answers.answer: Search chooses either the world deck or the discard pile for your pawn's region, never both. Discard-pile Search costs 2 Supply. World-deck Search costs 2 at zero Visions drawn, 3 at 1–2, and 4 at 3–5; Darkest Secret makes the world-deck cost 2, with other modifiers still applying. Draw 3 (or fewer if source runs out, a world-deck Vision stops you, or a modifier reduces draws); do not voluntarily stop early. Draw from world deck one card at a time; when a Vision appears, announce that a Vision was drawn, stop immediately, and advance Visions Drawn by 1. A Vision in a discard pile does not stop the draw or advance the track. No reshuffle is implied when a source empties.
answers.evidence: Actions, Search section: sources/costs and separate world-deck versus discard Vision handling.

answers.answer: Discard facedown onto the next region's pile in the cycle Cradle → Provinces → Hinterland → Cradle; for a hand/adviser discard, use the pile after the region of your pawn, never that same region. For a card discarded from a site in another region, use the cycle based on that card's region instead of your pawn's region. Favor on a discarded card immediately returns to its matching bank; secrets go to the acting player's board facedown.
answers.evidence: Search, Discard destinations paragraph: cycle and remote-site exception; resource handling.

answers.answer: You may have up to 3 advisers total, faceup and facedown combined; before going over, discard an adviser subject to locks. If the incoming card changes the adviser limit, check the new limit before playing it; with multiple limits use the lowest. A facedown adviser has no suit, restriction banner, or power; any card type, including a site-only card or Vision, can be held facedown. Later, playing or discarding a facedown adviser is a minor action; to play it faceup, use a legal destination and follow normal placement/play effects. A true Vision revealed by an Exile occupies the separate Revealed Vision space rather than an adviser slot; a newly revealed true Vision replaces and discards the old one. Chancellor/Citizens may hold true Visions facedown but cannot reveal them; Conspiracy can be played faceup by anyone and does not replace a true Vision.
answers.evidence: Search, Adviser and True Vision bullets; Minor actions, facedown adviser; Conspiracy paragraph.

answers.answer: Muster costs 1 Supply. Put 1 favor on an empty denizen or intact edifice at your pawn's site (no favor or secrets already) and gain 2 warbands from your personal bank onto your board; Citizens gain purple. It does not require rule; relics and ruins are ineligible, and no remote Muster is allowed. Trade costs 1 Supply and uses an empty denizen/intact edifice at your pawn's site. Option A: place 1 secret on it and gain 1 favor plus 1 per matching faceup adviser from that card's suit bank. Option B: place 2 favor on it and gain 1 shared-bank secret per matching faceup adviser. Facedown advisers never match; with no matching faceup advisers, option B gains zero secrets. Gains are limited by finite favor/warband supply; secrets are unlimited, but the costs remain payable even if the gain is zero.
answers.evidence: Actions, Muster and Trade sections: costs, eligible targets, outcomes, faceup matching, and source limits.

answers.answer: Recover costs 1 Supply plus the target cost. You may recover a facedown relic at your site, paying its printed site cost (3 favor to the indicated bank, burn 2 favor, burn 1 secret, or burn 2 secrets), then hold it faceup in your personal bank. Or recover either banner from anywhere, including yourself or the shared bank. For People's Favor, pay strictly more favor than it currently has; put the payment on it, distribute its old favor one at a time to suit banks in printed order starting from any chosen bank, and flip to normal if it was Mob. For Darkest Secret, pay strictly more secrets than it has; put payment on it, take 1 old secret for the new holder and give the rest to the previous holder (if recovering from yourself, all old secrets return to you; if from shared bank, remainder stays there). No seizure penalty applies to Recover.
answers.evidence: Actions, Recover: targets and relic costs; separate People's Favor and Darkest Secret payment/resource disposition bullets.

answers.answer: To recover Darkest Secret from another player, there must be at least one suited card at that player's pawn site whose suit matches none of that player's faceup advisers. One such card is enough even if others match. If the holder has no faceup advisers, a suited site card is unmatched and the banner is recoverable. An empty site or a ruin-only site protects it because neither supplies a suited card. Ruins and facedown advisers have no suit. Recovery from yourself or the shared bank ignores this protection.
answers.evidence: Darkest Secret protection, corrected by official errata paragraph.

answers.answer: A legal defender is any other player who rules your site or whose pawn is at your site. If no player rules your site, you may choose bandits. At least one target must be at your pawn's site; if the defender rules that site, you must target it. You may also target any of the defender's sites anywhere on the map, each adding 1 defense die. If defender's pawn is at your site, you may target their relic(s) using printed defense dice, their banner(s) using dice equal to banner resources, or their pawn and favor together for 2 dice. A relic target at the shared site itself satisfies the local-target requirement.
answers.evidence: Campaign steps 1–2: defender eligibility and declared targets, including remote and co-located relic cases.

answers.answer: Attacker selects up to as many attack dice as warbands in their attacking force, then applies relevant modifiers. Defense adds rolled shields (double-symbols multiply shields, stacking), all defending warbands at targeted sites, and defender's board force if their pawn is at the attacker site or a targeted site; bandits add 1 per targeted bandit site. Each attack skull immediately kills one of the attacker's force warbands. Count full swords and one additional attack per pair of hollow swords; a leftover hollow sword counts zero. The attacker may sacrifice surviving force warbands for +1 attack each, but if sacrificing must sacrifice exactly enough to win, no excess. Attacker must strictly exceed defense; a tie means defender wins.
answers.evidence: Campaign steps 2, 4, and 5: attack dice cap, defense total, skull/hollow sword rules, sacrifice and strict comparison.

answers.answer: On attacker victory, resolve defender defeat first: defender kills half its defending-force warbands rounded down and returns the rest to board; resolve defeated-plan effects. Then the attacker may place any number of surviving force warbands, including zero, on targeted sites; zero leaves a site to bandits unless another power applies. Take all targeted relics/banners. A banner seized by Campaign (unlike Recover) has 2 resources burned down to a minimum of 1; People's Favor flips to Mob. If pawn and favor were targeted, attacker may force defender to travel to a legal chosen site without Supply and may independently burn half the defender's board favor, rounded down. Respect travel restrictions; Shrouded Wood overrides destination choice if its enemy ruler chooses. Then resolve attacker's victorious plans. If defender wins, attacker targets are skipped and defender's victorious plans resolve. At end discard plans marked 'At end, discard.'
answers.evidence: Campaign steps 6–8: defeat before target resolution, zero garrison option, banner rule, banishment/favor, and plan timing.

answers.answer: If an Imperial player defends, Chancellor automatically joins as Ally; other non-attacking Citizens may join with defender's permission if their pawn is at attacker site or any targeted site. Defender/Allies' applicable modifiers and side-wide powers are shared, including Oathkeeper defense bonus; allied board warbands count only if their pawn is at attacker site or a target. They may use plans at Imperial sites and their own advisers, not another player's advisers; each shared plan is used once total, by one user who pays, and declared defender resolves order/priority disputes. Chancellor chooses which Imperial defending warbands die; surviving garrison warbands return to Chancellor's board while surviving Citizen board warbands stay there. A Citizen attacking Chancellor or another Citizen is non-Imperial for that Campaign. If Chancellor attacks a Citizen, that Citizen is non-Imperial for that Campaign. An intra-Empire Campaign does not strip all Citizens of Imperial status.
answers.evidence: Campaign defender-selection paragraph; Imperial defense bullets, especially shared powers, allies, plans, casualties, and status scope.

answers.answer: Base Travel costs by origin-to-destination region are: from Cradle, Cradle 1, Provinces 2, Hinterland 4; from Provinces, any region 2; from Hinterland, Cradle 4, Provinces 2, Hinterland 3. Travel may go to any different site, not just an adjacent slot. A facedown destination is revealed and stocked with its printed favor/secrets from shared bank and printed relic count from relic deck, facedown. Apply fixed-number cost first, then other increases/decreases; an applicable free-Travel power ('spend no Supply') is the final override and makes cost zero even after increases. Site entry restrictions still apply unless specifically ignored by a power.
answers.evidence: Travel section and cost-order paragraph: table, facedown reveal, fixed costs, modifiers, and free override.

answers.answer: The Grand Scepter holder may offer Citizenship to any Exile, including themself, but cannot use Scepter powers on the turn they took it; they also cannot make an offer on that turn. On a later turn an offer must promise exactly one Reliquary relic. They may additionally negotiate a binding exchange of favor, secrets, banners, and non-Reliquary relics, and may allow the recipient to peek at Reliquary relics. Acceptance flips the recipient to Citizen and replaces all their own board/map warbands with purple (if short, recipient chooses which to remove/replace), discards revealed Vision, flips their Usurper title to Oathkeeper, ends their Act if it is their turn, and refreshes full Supply. Then exchange promised pieces; Chancellor gains the uncovered mandatory Reliquary modifier. Forced Citizenship powers perform the conversion without an offer, relic gift, or invented exchange; only actual removal of a Reliquary relic uncovers its modifier. Separately, the Scepter holder can exile another Citizen by paying 5 favor adjusted +1 for recipient Oathkeeper/+1 recipient People's Favor/−1 payer Oathkeeper/−1 payer People's Favor (3–7 total); recipient changes board purple warbands to own color and refreshes full, while map garrisons remain purple. A Citizen without Scepter can self-exile by giving the Scepter holder favor equal to their board warbands plus all their secrets on board and denizen/relic/edifice cards; they flip Exile, change board warbands to own color, refresh full, and end Act. A Scepter-holding Citizen cannot self-exile.
answers.evidence: Citizenship and exile during play: Grand Scepter, Offer, Acceptance, Forced Citizenship, Exile another Citizen, and Self-exile paragraphs.

answers.answer: For the next Oath, a victory by Vision alone sets the next Oath to the one matching that Vision. Any other victory or multiple victory methods lets the winner choose any Oath except the current one. For Chronicle Citizenship, if the winner is an Exile, flip all Citizen boards, including boxed ones, to Exile; the winner may offer Chronicle Citizenship to other Exiles except those just flipped, but not themself. Each accepting Exile flips to Citizen and replaces every garrison at each site they rule with exactly one winner-color warband, regardless of previous garrison size. To rebuild the world deck, shuffle denizens remaining in play; the top stack is 10 denizens plus 2 random Visions (12 cards), the middle is 15 denizens plus the remaining 3 Visions (18 cards), and the remaining denizens go below. Thus it is not 14 cards: the aid's printed '12 denizens + 2' is explicitly incorrect.
answers.evidence: Writing the Chronicle, steps 1–2 and 9: Oath selection, free Chronicle Citizenship turnover/garrison exchange, and corrected deck stack counts.
